newsitem.title: CHILE: Brazil grants Chile same deal as Mercosur - Frei.
newsitem.headline: Brazil grants Chile same deal as Mercosur - Frei.

text.p: Chile will receive the same treatment as full members of the Mercosur trade bloc in a solution to the dispute sparked by Brazilian restrictions on import financing, said Chilean President Eduardo Frei.
"The government of Brazil has communicated to us officially a solution to the issue under which Chile will have the same treatment as all the countries in the Mercosur," Frei told reporters.
Chile became an associate member last year of the trade bloc which groups Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

A Chilean delegation, headed by Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia, will head to Brasilia Thursday "to talk with the Brazilian and Mercosur authorities so that we can participate together in any solution," said Frei.

The mission's objective "is to look for a solution, not for the short term, but the long term. An ad hoc commission of macroeconomic systems of the Mercosur will meet (to analyze this) and we are interested in taking part," he said.

Brazil's Finance Minister Pedro Malan announced on Wednesday preferential treatment for members of the Mercosur in relation to new import finance rules announced last week to slim Brazil's huge trade gap.
The pact exempts Mercosur imports from the new short-term financing restrictions if they are worth less than $40,000. The deal will be in force for 120 days.
Chile regards this 120-day period as a chance to negotiate for the complete lifting of the limitations, said acting Economy Minister Oscar Landerretche.
"The definitive solution is to lift the measures. We believe that the solution to this problem is possible within the Mercosur framework," he said.
Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said that Chile is studying the deal to see what impact it will have on exports to Brazil, worth close to $1 billion last year.
"We are not sure to what point it does or doesn't cover our needs or our principal problems. This is what we are investigating," said Insulza.
Garcia will be accompanied on his visit by Chile's top trade negotiator Juan Gabriel Valdes and a delegation of local businessmen.
Chilean business groups have estimated that exports worth between $200-250 million could be hurt by the restrictions.
Chile's top exports to Brazil include copper cathodes and concentrates, methanol, molybdenum and tomato paste.
